dedupe_keys.name: emergency food distribution in new orleans after hurricane ida 2021

description: This case examines how free food was distributed in New Orleans during the two weeks after Hurricane Ida made landfall on 29 August 2021. The authors compiled every free food distribution event they could find online into a list of sites with address, days and hours of operation and food offered, then mapped the sites and compared them with the social make-up of surrounding census tracts. The producers are Singleton, Chaparro, O'Malley, Fuster and Rose, publishing in Frontiers in Public Health (2022). Coverage is the city of New Orleans: 74 sites operated, 47.3 percent in tracts where more than 80 percent of residents are Black and 39.2 percent in tracts with more than 30 percent poverty; most offered prepared meals, over a third opened for only one day, and sites in high-poverty tracts more often started 7 to 15 days after the storm. The article is open access under CC BY. Caveats: the site list came from online sources and may miss informal or unadvertised distribution, and the site table is described but not released as a separate data set. Simulation uses: siting and timing of food aid points in post-disaster logistics models, and equity checks on access to emergency food. Related records: the National Academies post-hurricane supply chain study (case_study-post-hurricane-supply-chains-harvey-irma-maria) covers regional supply chains, and the USDA Food Access Research Atlas (data-usda-ers-food-access-research-atlas) maps normal food access.
